name: Sikorsky S-55 / H-19
summary: An early Sikorsky transport with the engine in the nose and the cockpit perched above it; still flown by a handful of tour operators, firefighters and collectors.

wings: Three-blade main rotor on a tall mast (five-blade on the quiet turbine conversions)
engines: Radial piston engine in the nose behind clamshell doors
Turbine conversions keep the engine in the nose, with different intakes and exhausts
fuselage: Bulbous rounded nose with the cockpit perched above the engine
Wheeled gear, with a high tail section and a four-post undercarriage
tail: Slim boom curving up to the tail rotor
Horizontal stabilizer low on the boom

tellTales: Radial engine in the nose with the cockpit perched above
Three-blade rotor over a bulbous round-nosed fuselage
Tailwheel gear and a slim tail boom

confusedWith.howToTell: The S-58 is larger with a four-blade rotor and a longer boxy fuselage; the S-55 has three blades and a smaller body.
The S-61 has two turbines on the roof and a boat-shaped hull; the S-55 has an engine in the nose.
The Huey has a turbine on top, a slim nose and a two-blade rotor; the S-55 has three blades and a bulbous nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
